label.trigger: Any path-producing call (normalize, join, get_absolute, get_relative, change_root, change_basename, change_extension, change_segment) whose complete result is exactly as long as the buffer_size it was given, for instance joining "ab" and "cd" into a 5-byte buffer, so the end position equals buffer_size.
label.expected_impact: The final NUL is stored at index buffer_size, one byte beyond the caller's buffer, and the last byte inside the buffer keeps a path character. The caller ends up with an unterminated string plus a one-byte out-of-bounds write, so later strlen/strcmp/printf on the result read past the buffer, contrary to the documented truncation promise.

anchors.start: * This function creates a normalized version of the path within the specified
anchors.end: * (excluding the null-terminating character). The path may be the same memory

context_locations.note: The public header defines buffer_size as the whole capacity including the terminator and promises a NUL inside it even when the text is cut short; the same promise is repeated for every writer in the API.
Writers fill the buffer up to its last byte and return the untruncated length, so the position handed to the terminating helper can be equal to or larger than buffer_size.
Typical caller: it passes the total output length as the position, which equals the capacity when the normalized path fits with no room left for the NUL.

known_counterevidence.note: Copying right up to the final byte of the buffer looks like it leaves no room for the NUL, but that is by design: the terminating step overwrites the last byte whenever the text did not fit. A finding about the copy clamp is not this defect.

label.fix_summary: Treat a position equal to buffer_size like a larger one: use the greater-or-equal comparison so the NUL goes into buffer[buffer_size - 1] whenever no slot is left after the text.
distinctive_tokens: exactly as long as the buffer_size

check.summary: Builds the library and its own test runner with CMake and runs the full suite; the existing normalize/terminated test walks small buffer sizes and requires a NUL at the last usable index, which fails when the output length equals the buffer size.

verification.summary: verify --run-checks with cmake 4.2.3 and gcc 15.2.0 (project flags, -Werror, no sanitizer): on before the suite exits non-zero and reports normalize/terminated as FAILURE; on the pinned commit it exits 0 without that line. A scratch build of the same trees showed 179/180 passing with the patch and 180/180 without. The one-byte write lands inside the test's FILENAME_MAX array, so detection comes from the test's content assertion, not from a sanitizer. No external dependencies.
